Russia pounds Kyiv with missiles and drones, hours after agreeing to peace talks

Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones toward Moscow overnight as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest U.S. push to end the conflict.

Russia said Wednesday it was ready to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, after President Vladimir Putin hosted U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in St. Petersburg.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he hoped negotiations, which would be the first since February, would take place early in November.

Ukraine said Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles in three waves. Russia said Ukraine launched 630 drones toward the capital, Moscow, during the night.

The two sides held an exchange of war dead, with Moscow handing over 252 bodies and Ukraine handing over 25, according to the Belta state news agency in neighboring Belarus. Such exchanges have accompanied moves toward talks in the past.

But while Witkoff spoke of "some degree of momentum" after meeting Zelenskyy and European and NATO officials in Oslo earlier in the week, the Kremlin expressed doubts.

"The Americans sensed some new nuances [in Oslo] and told us about this. But these nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said.

Russia says it launched the war, the deadliest in Europe since World War II, in part to prevent Ukraine from joining NATO. It has repeatedly said it would not end fighting unless Ukraine cedes more land, limits the size of its forces and is permanently barred from forming alliances.

Ukraine, which says the invasion was an unprovoked war of conquest, has long dismissed Russia's conditions as a demand for capitulation that would leave it defenseless against future Russian attacks.

Zelenskyy's meeting with Witkoff was aimed in part at smoothing over a deterioration in relations with Washington this month, after President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and lifted sanctions on Moscow.

Kyiv says Washington failed to provide early-warning data on Russian missile launches, throttled the SpaceX satellite system used to guide Ukrainian drones, and withheld missile defense systems bought on its behalf by Europeans. Washington denies any shift in policy to intentionally hamper Ukraine's forces.

Trump has repeatedly rebuked Ukraine for attacking Russian oil refineries while saying little about far deadlier Russian attacks on Ukraine. He called for Zelenskyy to be replaced and said Russia's actions in Ukraine have been "fine."

Zelenskyy, who long avoided any criticism of the Trump administration, has increasingly pushed back against what he describes as a shift toward sympathy with Moscow.

On Thursday Zelenskyy snapped back at Witkoff for saluting Putin as a "humanitarian" during his visit to Russia, when the U.S. envoy thanked Putin for releasing a 74-year-old American captured by Russian forces in Ukraine.

"Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian 'humanitarians' since yesterday evening," Zelenskyy posted on X. "They used 21 missiles. Unfortunately, numerous sites across the city have been hit and damaged."

He said two people were killed and 34 injured, including five children, in attacks on a dozen Ukrainian regions.

Russia said it carried out a "massive strike" overnight on port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, as well as on vessels used by the Ukrainian military.

In Russia, two people were wounded near Moscow by drones launched toward the capital during the night, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. Most of the drones were downed at long range, he added.

In the Russian border region of Belgorod, one man was killed and another wounded by Ukrainian drones, local officials said.

With the front lines of the war largely static, both sides have escalated long-range airstrikes this year. Russia has particularly targeted the Ukrainian power grid, while Ukraine has aimed at Russian oil refineries. Both have struck data centers, commercial warehouses and Black Sea shipping.

The war has ground on for more than 4-1/2 years, defying Trump's pledge during his 2024 election campaign that he could end it in a day. No breakthrough emerged from three short meetings in Istanbul last year and three rounds of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi and Geneva at the start of this year.
